sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
St. Gallen has made street parking in the centre dearer, and the charges are now contested. Since 1 January 2022, about 600 public surface spaces in the centre have been charged every day and night rather than only in working hours, at CHF 2.00 an hour by day and CHF 1.50 at night and on Sundays. The city said the aim was to use spaces more appropriately and make underground garages more attractive [0]. From 1 November 2024 the daytime rate on white-zone spaces in the centre rose from CHF 2.00 to CHF 2.50, and a night and Sunday rate of CHF 1.00 was introduced outside the centre [2]. The Swiss Price Supervisor had recommended on 20 March 2024 cutting Extended Blue Zone fees by 37% and white-zone fees by 59% and dropping the increases. He also noted that only 455 of 2,800 garage spaces (16%) are publicly managed, and treated garage prices as outside his remit [1]. The Extended Blue Zone requires a permit around the clock, with resident permits at CHF 30 to 40 a month and commuter permits at CHF 150 to 160 [4].

Two initiatives are now pending. On 25 August 2026 the Stadtparlament rejected the 'Parkgebühr-Initiative' by 38 votes to 20 [6], and the Stadtrat set the popular vote for 28 February 2027, which has not happened yet [7]. A second initiative from the same association, which reached its 1,000 signatures, asks for a 'moderate number' of above-ground spaces in the centre and old town 'at the level of around 2015' [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Garage prices vary widely, and a news report in May 2026 described a 'wild patchwork', citing CHF 2 an hour at Brühltor and Burggraben, CHF 2.60 at the station, CHF 2.40 at the town hall and a half-hour system at Neumarkt [8]. Indigo Suisse took over the historic Neumarkt car park on 1 April 2025, with a remote management centre [11], and it operates Parkhaus Central with 614 spaces, listed at CHF 2.00 for the first hour and CHF 20 for 24 hours [10]. The publicly run Kreuzbleiche garage is being renovated from June 2026 to May 2027, with limited parking in the meantime [22].

A shared guidance system, run by a company owned by private garage operators and the city, shows free spaces at 13 facilities [13]. The Parkleitsystem lists Neumarkt with 274 publicly managed spaces and 10 charging stations at CHF 1.50 per 30 minutes in the first hour, up to CHF 25 a day [12], and the station garage at CHF 2.60 an hour by day with day passes of CHF 25 [14]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our St. Gallen data cover ten car parks with 2,045 spaces. Five are within 500 m of the Bohl (1,035 spaces) and five more within 1 km (1,010). City Parking St. Gallen AG runs Bahnhof and Brühltor [14][15], Indigo runs Neumarkt [12], and Einstein belongs to Wildegg Immobilien AG, at CHF 2.50 an hour around the clock [16]. Capacities in our feed differ from the Parkleitsystem's publicly managed counts, for example Einstein at 187 against 126, so percentages should be read with care.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 38% on weekdays and 30% at weekends. The fullest are the small Rathaus garage (54% on weekdays, 53% at weekends), Stadtpark (52%, falling to 26% at weekends) and the station garage (48%, 28%). Burggraben is at 44% and Einstein at 43%. The emptiest are Brühltor (23%, the largest at 448 spaces), Raiffeisenzentrum (26%, 7% at weekends) and Spisertor (28%). Within 500 m the average is 34%, against 41% for the five between 500 m and 1 km. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for St. Gallen.
